captions.detailed: This 3D model is a thick-walled hollow cylinder designed as a test object, featuring a triangular inner profile. The outer surface of the cylinder is patterned with multiple tiers of small, spherical dimples arranged in vertical columns. These columns of dimples are offset from one another horizontally between adjacent tiers, creating a staggered pattern around the circumference.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric cylinder with a triangular inner hollow core for 3D printer testing. The outer shell should feature a configurable number of vertical tiers of spherical dimples, with each tier rotated to stagger the dimples relative to the one below it, and parameters to control the cylinder radius, wall thickness, dimple depth, and the number of tiers.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a boolean difference operation. An outer cylinder primitive is hollowed out by subtracting a slightly taller inner cylinder (or a triangular profile representation). To create the dimples, two separate for-loops iterate through the tiers and the number of dimples per tier, rotating and translating sphere primitives along the outer surface of the cylinder to subtract them from the main body. The dimples in the second loop are offset by an angular rotation of 180 degrees divided by the number of dimples per tier to achieve the staggered pattern.
